Ukraine Takes First Step Toward Joining Single Euro Payment Area — Ukraine’s parliament passed a bill on joining the Single Euro Payment Area (SEPA) in its first reading on Nov. 10. The Finance Ministry says membership will speed up payments and save the Ukrainian economy €70-100 million in banking fees. The bill also raises the financial monitoring threshold and is a condition for EU and World Bank support.

Russia’s 400,000 Confirmed Troop Losses – a Detailed Breakdown — Leaked Rosstat data of death certificates obtained by hacker groups have shed light on confirmed Russian war deaths, estimated at around 450,000. The data shows the Muslim republic of Bashkortostan taking the brunt of war deaths, with eastern Ukraine’s Donetsk witnessing over half of the overall deaths since Moscow’s 2022 invasion began.

Abu Dhabi Talks Put Major Ukraine-Russia POW Swap on the Table — A major prisoner exchange is among the issues discussed at the Abu Dhabi negotiations, according to sources cited by RBC-Ukraine. The two-day talks also address security guarantees and the future European security architecture, with the next round scheduled for Nov. 11.

Russia Sends FSB Chief to Face Budanov at Peace Talks After His Unit Was Linked to Plot to Kill Him — Dmitry Minayev, who heads an FSB department linked by Ukrainian officials to a 2019 attempt to kill Kyrylo Budanov, has joined Russia’s delegation for talks with Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi.

Abu Dhabi Talks Cover Security Guarantees for Russia — Ukraine, Russia, and the US discussed security guarantees for Kyiv and Europe, alongside Moscow’s demands for guarantees of its own, according to a source cited by Ukrainska Pravda on Tuesday. Ukraine’s delegation insisted that the war must stop before a broader European security framework can be developed. The talks also addressed Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction.

UN Official: Russian Weapons Are Killing Ukrainian Civilians Faster Than Ever — UN official Kayoko Gotoh told the Security Council Russian attacks killed 328 civilians and injured 2,105 in September, up 85% year-on-year. October casualties remained similarly high; UN figures since February 2022: 17,968 dead, 57,713 injured.

US Urges Russia to Let Europe Join Ukraine Talks — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will press Russia to accept direct European participation in future Ukraine peace negotiations, Politico reported on Tuesday. European officials are already holding separate consultations in Abu Dhabi, but Washington wants them involved in the main talks. The proposal adds urgency to Europe’s unresolved debate over who should represent it.

France Accuses Iran of Europe-Wide Industrial Fridge Hack — After a cyberattack hit industrial fridges across Europe and reportedly spoiled millions of euros worth of food in mid-October, France has accused a hacker unit affiliated with Tehran of responsibility. Another wave of similar cyberattacks followed weeks later against other European countries, though it remains unclear whether the two waves are related, and the perpetrator of the second wave remains unclear.

Russia Hits Epicentr K Mall in Kropyvnytskyi, 2 Injured — A Russian attack hit an Epicentr K shopping center in Kropyvnytskyi on Tuesday morning, injuring two people and starting a fire after a repeat strike. The retailer, Ukraine’s largest home improvement chain, has faced a wave of attacks since August that destroyed malls in Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, Kyiv, and Kharkiv and its last major logistics hub in Khmelnytskyi.

Exclusive: Russia Preparing Strikes on Ukraine’s Food Industry, Intel Source Says — Russia is preparing attacks on Ukrainian and foreign-owned food industry facilities in Ukraine to undermine food security, damage the economy and expand its share of agricultural export markets, a Ukrainian military intelligence source told Kyiv Post exclusively.

Netherlands to Provide Naftogaz With €23M for Additional Gas Purchases — Ukraine’s gas conglomerate Naftogaz has signed a €23 million grant agreement with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), with funding from the Dutch government. The funds will go towards additional gas purchases during peak consumption periods. Naftogaz’s acting CEO said Ukraine has enough reserves for the winter, but additional supplies could provide an extra safety margin.

Zelensky: Putin Will Return in 1, 2 or 5 Years if Ukraine Gives Up Donbas — Zelensky warned that surrendering the Donbas would only give Russia time to regroup before attacking again. He said a ceasefire along current front lines, followed by negotiations, offers the fastest path to ending the war.

Neither Side May Be Able to Win This War | Stefan Korshak — Ukraine will seek a ceasefire in trilateral talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi, but Kyiv Post correspondent Korshak expects no concrete agreements. Russia’s territorial and NATO-related demands remain major obstacles, while European support remains vital to Ukraine’s defense.

Denmark Announces €643 Million Military Aid Package for Ukraine — Denmark announced its 32nd military aid package for Ukraine, worth 4.8 billion Danish kroner, as President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Copenhagen.

Bulgaria Motorway Pileup Kills 11, Dozens Injured — At least 11 people were killed and 48 injured in motorway pileups involving around 50 vehicles near Yambol, southeastern Bulgaria, amid thick fog. Bulgaria recorded the EU’s highest road fatality rate in 2025, with 71 deaths per million people.

Modified Trawler Pitched as Royal Navy Russian Sub Hunter — Norway’s Kongsberg Maritime unveiled its “Arctic Hunter” uncrewed surface vessel (USV), converted from a commercial trawler, to track Russian submarines. It is intended to operate in the Arctic and North Atlantic as part of the UK navy’s hybrid fleet concept – the pairing of uncrewed vessels with conventional warships.

Russian Drone Attack Kills 2 in Western Ukraine’s Ladyzhyn — Russian drones killed two people in the city of Ladyzhyn in western Ukraine’s Vinnytsia region on Nov. 10. The attack damaged civilian infrastructure, while energy facilities and a civilian enterprise were also hit in the region. Ladyzhyn declared three days of mourning.

Zelensky Seeks Air Defenses at Nordic Talks in Denmark — President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Denmark to discuss military assistance, air defenses, and energy infrastructure security with Nordic leaders. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen urged continued support for Ukraine amid Russian attacks on civilians and essential services. The visit coincides with US-mediated negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow in Abu Dhabi.

Russian Drone Hits Sumy Train as Crew Takes Shelter — A Russian drone struck a commuter train standing at a railway station in Sumy on Nov. 10, Ukrainian officials said. No passengers were aboard, and the crew was in shelter, preventing casualties. City authorities also reported damage to a locomotive cab and an industrial building during the morning’s attacks, as Russia continues targeting Ukraine’s rail network.

Kasparov Cancels Berlin Trip After Warnings of Assassination — Exiled Russian opposition figure Garry Kasparov canceled his appearance at Berlin Freedom Week after security experts warned of a possible Russian assassination plot. The former chess champion, previously alerted by US and Lithuanian authorities, criticized European officials for failing to counter Kremlin threats.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Aircraft Repair Facility Overnight — Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Russia’s Novgorod Oblast, which services military transport aircraft and A-50 airborne early warning planes. The extent of the damage is being assessed, but the strike could delay aircraft repairs and their return to service.

Can Abu Dhabi Talks Bring Ukraine Closer to Peace? First Round Ends After 4.5 Hours — Ukraine, the US, and Russia concluded the first day of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi after 4.5 hours, with the next round scheduled for Nov. 11. Zelensky has spoken briefly with the Ukrainian delegation and plans a more detailed discussion later.

Ukraine Opens Abu Dhabi Talks With Western Partners Ahead of Russia Meeting — Ukrainian negotiators opened consultations with US and European partners to coordinate positions before planned trilateral talks with Russia. Kyiv’s priorities include ending the fighting, securing reliable postwar security guarantees, supporting economic recovery, and addressing humanitarian issues.

Zelensky Ready to Meet Putin 'Even in Antarctica,' Ukraine's UN Envoy Says — Zelensky is ready to meet Putin anywhere except Moscow, including Antarctica, Ukraine's UN envoy said. Melnyk also accused Russia of exploiting diplomacy to prolong the war and urged UN members to provide Ukraine with more air defense systems.

Fuel Sales Limited Across Russian Regions amid Ukrainian Refinery Strikes — Several Russian regions have introduced fuel purchase limits at petrol stations amid renewed Ukrainian strikes on the country’s refineries. Rosneft stations have reportedly restricted sales in at least four regions, with limits varying by fuel type and location.

Toporowski: ‘Being in Kyiv Is My Duty’ — Marek Toporowski, one of Poland’s leading performers of historically informed music, discusses musical freedom, cultural identity, reclaiming national musical heritage, and why he considers performing in Kyiv a duty and a sign of solidarity.

Russia, Ukraine Reportedly Show Private Flexibility on Territory Ahead of Talks — Russia and Ukraine have privately shown some flexibility on a possible territorial exchange ahead of Abu Dhabi talks, according to a US official. Negotiations will also address security guarantees for Ukraine, potentially including a NATO-style Article 5 commitment.

Von der Leyen Demands Ukraine Ceasefire Before Talks on Europe’s Security — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said broader negotiations over Europe’s security architecture must wait until Russia agrees to a ceasefire in Ukraine. Speaking alongside Romanian President Nicușor Dan in Bucharest, she announced €50 million for a Black Sea Maritime Security Hub and €10 million for search-and-rescue operations. Dan warned that Russia was attempting to draw European countries into its wa

US Lawmakers Demand Hegseth Speed Up $400M Ukraine Aid — A bipartisan group of 32 US lawmakers has demanded that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth accelerate delivery of $400 million in congressionally approved military aid to Ukraine. In a letter also addressed to White House budget chief Russell Vought, lawmakers warned that the Pentagon’s current schedule extends through fiscal year 2029, after President Donald Trump’s term ends.

Trump Hails Peace Talks, Brushes Off Putin Ignoring Ceasefire Demands — US President Donald Trump expressed optimism about negotiations between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, saying both sides appeared increasingly willing to end the war. However, during a surprise White House press conference, he dismissed a reporter’s question about Russian President Vladimir Putin repeatedly ignoring his ceasefire demands. Trump also boasted of record US weapons production as Ukraine reported unprecedented

Rubio Threatens ‘Tremendous Damage’ to ICC Unless Court Bows to US Demands — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that Washington could inflict “tremendous damage” on the International Criminal Court unless it changes its approach to prosecuting nationals of nonmember states. The warning raises questions about the future of a court that has issued arrest warrants for Russian President Vladimir Putin and senior Russian military officials over alleged war crimes in Ukraine.

Russian Shahed Drones Strike Kharkiv, Injuring 6 and Setting House Ablaze — Russian Shahed drones struck residential areas of Kharkiv on Monday evening, injuring at least six people. A private house caught fire and approximately 10 vehicles were damaged, according to Mayor Ihor Terekhov.

Trump’s Pentagon Chief Faces Impeachment Over Iran War — Republican Congressman Thomas Massie formally introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of illegally conducting the Iran war and abusing his authority. The move comes after Democrats won control of both chambers in the midterms and prepare broader investigations into the Trump administration.

Zelensky Says Russia Wants to Divide Ukraine Along Dnipro, Pledges State Resources to Frontline Regions — Following a meeting attended by authorities from five frontline regions and Kyiv, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday, Nov. 9 that Russia is trying to divide Ukraine along the Dnipro River through its strikes on bridges and the power grid. He said that central government is ready to send additional resources wherever local authorities cannot cope, while urging all levels of governmen

EU Extends Ukraine Military Training Mission to 2028 With Nearly €300M in Funding — European Union (EU) member states agreed on Monday, Nov. 9, to extend their military training mission for Ukraine to Nov. 15, 2028. The programme will be backed with nearly €300 million ($335 million) in fresh funding. For the first time since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale war, Brussels will set up the European Union Military Assistance Mission in support of Ukraine (EUMAM), with the training also leaning

Komyshuvakha, Mariupol Theater Strikes To Serve as War Crimes Evidence — Speaking during a UN Security Council meeting on Monday, Nov. 9, Ukraine’s Ambassador to the UN Andrii Melynk said Russia’s bombing of a school in Komyshuvakha and its 2022 strike on the Mariupol Drama Theater will be used as war crimes evidence against those who planned, ordered and carried out the attacks. In addition, he criticized the UN for appointing a Russian diplomat to oversee mine action, saying Moscow made Ukrain

Russian Military Tests Cruise Missile Launches from Aerial Platforms — Russia’s Ministry of Defense has published videos and images of a modified “Orion” unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) along with Mi-8AMTSh-VN and Mi-28NM Attack helicopters carrying long-range cruise missiles and jet-powered drones. These will potentially provide Russia with a vastly increased battlefield range.
NVIDIA, AMD, Intel: Inside the Chips Powering Russia’s War — Former SEAL Team Six Squadron Leader Chuck Pfarrer takes a deep dive into the supply chain behind Russia’s terror weapons.

Zelensky, Modi Discuss Black Sea Food Corridors Ahead of Abu Dhabi Talks — President Volodymyr Zelensky spoke with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, Nov. 9, ahead of the trilateral talks with Russia and the US on Nov. 10-11. Zelensky urged New Delhi to identify steps it could take to help end Russia’s war, while India appeared ready to mediate in establishing Black Sea food corridors. So far, Russia has rejected all proposals for a Black Sea grain deal, even as attacks on shipping c

Russia Transfers Detained OSCE Staff Member to Medical Correctional Facility, Ukraine Says — Russia has transferred Vadym Golda, a Ukrainian staff member of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) to a medical correctional facility in Russia’s Tambov region, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Monday, Nov. 9. If confirmed, Golda would be the third OSCE employee moved from occupied Ukraine to Russia in violation of the Geneva Conventions, Sybiha pointed out, noting that

The World Has a Lot to Learn From Krakow — Journalist Lesia Dubenko describes hearing gunfire in central Krakow and witnessing the aftermath. Beyond the attacker’s motives, she argues, the response of police, medical workers and ordinary residents deserves attention.

Oleshky Ceasefire: How Russia Exploited It, and What Now? — Ukraine's Oleshky evacuation operation rescued several hundred civilians from Russian occupation but failed to achieve its broader humanitarian goals. It allowed Russian forces to exploit the five-day ceasefire to reinforce their positions on the left bank of the Dnipro River. Ukraine has acknowledged the subsequent Russian military buildup, raising questions about the operation's strategic costs and the fate of more than 1,000 civilian

Trump Doubles Down — Fresh from a Democratic midterm landslide, Donald Trump has promoted Stephen Miller, architect of his hardline policies, to White House Chief of Staff, signaling no shift on Ukraine, Iran, or Cuba. A day later, Trump touted a “big, beautiful agreement” to end Russia’s war, only for the Kremlin to say Putin had no details. With Putin short on money and manpower, Trump still refuses to use sanctions as leverage and keeps getting outplayed.

Germany Threatens EU Budget Veto Over Ukraine Funding — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to block the EU’s next seven-year budget unless all member states commit to financing Ukraine in 2027 and beyond, the Financial Times reported. His demand links the bloc’s wider spending negotiations to Kyiv’s urgent funding needs, as several governments resist further contributions and Germany seeks a lasting agreement.

‘Send the Chocolate One Ahead’: Russian Commander Orders African Recruit Into ‘Kill Zone’ — An intercepted conversation records a Russian commander ordering a soldier to send an African recruit about 20 meters ahead through a dangerous area, according to Ukraine’s military intelligence.

Coalition of the Willing Kicks Off War Drills for Ukraine’s Postwar Deployment — The UK- and France-led Coalition of the Willing on Monday kicked off its Exercise Koalicja in Poland, with 2,800 troops from 11 nations involved, set to last until Nov. 22, to prepare for planned troop deployments to postwar Ukraine. Russia has previously rejected the proposals.

19 People May Be Trapped in Underground School Shelter Leveled by Russian Bombs — Up to 19 people may still be trapped under rubble in Komyshuvakha after a Russian airstrike. Rescuers have recovered 55 bodies, while Russian drone attacks on the rescue operation injured two SES personnel on Sunday, Nov. 8.

Canada Imposes New Sanctions on Russia to Curb Missile Capabilities — Canada has announced additional sanctions against Russia, adding 38 entities and 24 individuals to its sanctions list. The measures target elements of Russia’s defense industry involved in ballistic missile technology, as well as cyber activities and financial networks that help sustain the country’s war economy. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said the restrictions are intended to undermine Moscow’s ability to strike Uk

Ukraine Heads to Abu Dhabi for Talks as Umerov Vows to Keep Europe Involved — Ukraine's delegation has departed for Abu Dhabi for two days of trilateral talks with the US and Russia. Kyiv will also hold separate meetings with representatives of four European countries, NATO, and the European Commission.

The Berlin Wall Didn’t Fall Entirely in 1989 – Ukraine Is Completing the Job — An important symbolic victory was gained over Soviet Russian communism back then, but Moscow has since renewed its rapacious aggression, and the frontline in Ukraine is the new Berlin Wall.

Ukraine Drone Forces Shift to Starlink Alternative for Comms to Hit Russia — Ukraine may be adopting Israeli-Italian HiSKY satellite links for deep-strike drones, trading Starlink’s capacity in exchange for greater resistance to jamming and US interference. Use remains unconfirmed, but recent refinery strikes suggest improved accuracy and effectiveness.

Ukraine Faces Another Year of Patriot Missile Shortages as European Stocks Run Low – Bloomberg — European countries are reluctant to transfer scarce Patriot interceptors to Ukraine without firm US commitments to replenish their stocks. Deliveries from European production are expected to begin easing the shortage in about a year.

US Launches ‘Iron Gate’ to Cut Iran’s Weapons Supply Routes — The US military has established Task Force Iron Gate to disrupt weapons shipments, sanctioned goods, and illicit financing moving through Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea. The approximately 20-person team will coordinate with other US agencies, extending pressure beyond the naval blockade. The announcement comes as Washington and Tehran remain divided over conditions for renewed peace talks.

Kyiv to Host the Ninth International Fintech Conference, UAFIN.TECH 2026 — Kyiv will host UAFIN.TECH 2026 on Dec. 4, bringing together Ukrainian and international experts to discuss Agentic Banking. The conference will explore how autonomous AI systems could reshape banking, financial services, cybersecurity and customer experience.

Ukraine Backs Space Forces Bill to Counter Missile Threats — Ukraine’s parliament has approved the first reading of legislation to establish Space Forces within the Armed Forces, with 252 lawmakers voting in favor. The initiative supports plans for independent missile launch detection, stronger defenses against missile threats, and secure satellite communications. The vote advances the proposal but does not constitute final adoption or establish an operational force.

Record Number of Russians Head for the Exit Amid New Draft Fears — More than 1.13 million Russians traveled to Georgia, Armenia and Serbia between July and September 2026, the highest figure in 17 years. The surge comes amid growing fears of another mobilization campaign, as Russia struggles to meet military recruitment targets and Ukrainian intelligence reports preparations for a potential new draft.

Ukraine, Finland Launch €300M Joint Defense Projects — Ukraine and Finland are expanding cooperation in defense production through a package of projects worth approximately €300 million. The countries signed seven documents, three of them related to the defense industry, during a meeting involving President Volodymyr Zelensky and representatives of Ukrainian and Finnish defense companies. The package includes €200 million under the Drone Deal and €100 million through the Build with Ukraine initi

Territorial Changes: Kremlin Says Ukraine ‘Already a Different Country’ — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov claimed Ukraine was already geographically a different country, citing “realities on the ground” after US President Donald Trump suggested a peace deal could alter Ukraine’s territorial boundaries. Moscow continues to demand recognition of its claims over occupied Ukrainian territories, including areas still under Kyiv’s control.

Police Detain Former Hungarian PM Orban’s Brother — Aron Orban was taken into custody as part of a human trafficking investigation involving an alleged visa-for-money scheme. Former Prime Minister Viktor Orban called the detention a politically motivated attempt to target him. The case is part of a broader accountability drive following Magyar’s election victory and the end of Orban’s 16-year rule.

Russia Faces Sabotage Epidemic That Mirrors Own Hybrid Assault on Europe — As Russia steps up its hybrid war attacks on Europe, Moscow is experiencing a surge in sabotage incidents on its own territory. OSINT analysis identified a seven-fold increase in attacks since the start of its 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Will a Freezing Winter Save Ukraine from Russian Drones? — As Russia ramps up its use of jet-powered drones against Ukraine, questions remain over whether harsh winter conditions could limit their effectiveness. Valerii Zarubin, CEO of BlueBird Tech, explains how freezing temperatures, icing, and adverse weather affect drone operations – and why Ukraine must strengthen its defenses rather than rely on the cold to slow Russian attacks.

Russian Strike on Odesa Infrastructure Facility Kills 3, Injures 1 — Russian forces struck an infrastructure facility in Odesa on Monday, Nov. 9, killing three people and seriously injuring another. The attack came two days after a separate Russian strike killed one person and damaged municipal infrastructure in the city.

Russian Network Used French Riots to Spread Anti-Migrant Lies — A covert Russian network spread fabricated reports about migrants and sought to undermine France's government during last month's riots, an EU assessment found. Separate French findings showed MAGA-linked and Israeli accounts generated tens of millions of views with hostile narratives about the unrest.

Russian FPV Drone Strike Injures 3 Ukrenergo Workers in Sumy — A Russian FPV drone struck a vehicle carrying Ukrenergo employees in Sumy on the morning of Nov. 9, injuring three. The attack comes days after one of Russia’s largest assaults on the energy sector this year and as Kyiv warns of more strikes on power and bridges.

IMF Mission Lands in Kyiv for November 2026 Review — An International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission arrived in Kyiv on Monday to conduct a combined second and third review of Ukraine’s program. A successful assessment is critical to unlock donor support and cover a $32.6 billion non-military budget shortfall.

EU Divided Over European Role in Upcoming Ukraine-Russia Talks — National security advisers from the E3 countries will attend the Nov. 10-11 talks, but Italy and Poland want a wider European role in discussions expected to address the continent’s future security architecture. Germany has outlined four principles for a potential peace settlement, including ending the war before discussing Europe’s security order.

‘What Have I Done?’ Trump Dismisses Impeachment Prospect — Donald Trump said he could not imagine Democrats impeaching him again, defending his record in an interview broadcast after Republicans lost control of Congress. Democrats are preparing investigations into his administration, while House leader Hakeem Jeffries has separately backed impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Trump was impeached twice during his first term and acquitted both times.

US Electronics Found in Russia’s New Geran-5 Weapon Capable of Reaching 1,000 Kph — Ukraine’s military intelligence says Russia’s new Geran-5 K5-K contains 93 foreign electronic components, including 52 from US manufacturers. Smaller than its predecessor, the jet-powered weapon carries a 90-kilogram warhead, has a reported range of 1,000 kilometers and cruises at more than 450 kph, with speeds reaching 1,000 kph during certain maneuvers.

EU to Use Emergency Aid Mechanism for Ukraine — The EU will use a special emergency assistance mechanism to accelerate funding for Ukraine’s most urgent needs, President Volodymyr Zelensky said after speaking with Ursula von der Leyen. The agreement comes as Russian strikes disrupt electricity, water, and heating supplies. The leaders also discussed winter aid, EU accession, and preparations for talks in Abu Dhabi.

Estonia Calls Russian Sabotage ‘State Terrorism’ as Cyberattacks Hit Supermarkets — Estonia’s interior minister has urged Europe to classify Russian sabotage as state-sponsored terrorism. His warning comes amid cyberattacks affecting nearly 100 supermarkets across Europe and a wider rise in suspected Russian-linked acts of sabotage.

A Mother’s Campaign for Ukrainian Sons Captured by Russia — Tetiana Vyshniak, known as “Mama Tania,” spent four years campaigning for the release of her son Artem, an Azovstal defender captured by Russian forces during the 2022 siege of Mariupol. After more than 400 rallies, he was finally freed. But with hundreds of Azov fighters and thousands of other Ukrainians still held by Russia, Vyshniak continues her daily fight for their return, standing alongside families still waiting for their loved

Mélenchon Accused of Echoing Kremlin Propaganda on Ukraine — French far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon faces backlash after suggesting that residents of Ukrainian territories should vote on any land concessions under a peace deal, with critics accusing him of repeating Kremlin talking points ahead of France’s 2027 presidential election.

Trump: Ukraine Will Have ‘Different Shape’ After War, Peace Deal Is Near — Trump says Ukraine will emerge from Russia’s war with a “little bit different shape,” hints at territorial changes under a future peace deal, and defends easing Russian diesel restrictions as US-mediated negotiations prepare to resume in Abu Dhabi.

Ukraine Strikes Russia’s Second-Largest Oil Refinery and Iskander Missile Fuel Plant — Ukrainian forces targeted two key Russian facilities near St. Petersburg on Nov. 9: the country’s second-largest oil refinery and a plant producing solid rocket propellant for Iskander ballistic missiles. Russia reported 113 drones over the region, while Ukraine’s General Staff confirmed damage to three production workshops at the Morozov Plant.

US, Armenia and Azerbaijan Launch Planning Group for Trump Peace Route — The US, Armenia and Azerbaijan have launched trilateral technical meetings to advance the 43-kilometre TRIPP corridor across southern Armenia. Initial discussions will focus on transportation and electricity transmission. The US-backed project aims to connect Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan and Turkey, strengthen trade links between Asia and Europe, and reshape regional connectivity while reducing reliance on Russia and Iran.

The Story NATO Needs to Tell — The Right and Left-wing establishments are wrong about the alliance. NATO membership is not a luxury, but a shield against national extinction. Aspiring members can play a major role in changing that perception.

Whether it’s military updates, political changes, or international reactions — we bring you the latest Ukraine news as it happens. All reports are carefully curated from verified sources and KyivPost correspondents on the ground

The Re-Introduction of Ukrainian GCSE Is a Victory for Our Children, and a Promise to Ukraine’s Future — Ukrainians who flee the war and come to live in Britain should have the chance to get credit for their knowledge of Ukrainian. Up till now they could only get a General Certificate of Secondary Education in Russian. Now Ukrainian GCSE is being re-introduced.

Nadia Svitlychna at 90: A Life of Courage, Dignity and Solidarity — On the 90th anniversary of Nadia Svitlychna’s birth, I remember my friend and colleague’s quiet courage, warmth and unwavering solidarity with those persecuted for their beliefs. From Soviet imprisonment to human rights advocacy and Radio Liberty broadcasts, she defended Ukrainian identity and preserved the voices of her fellow dissidents. I feel privileged to have known her and her brother Ivan. Their example remains vital as U

US Offers $20M Reward for Intel on Iran’s Nuclear Program — The US Department of State’s Rewards for Justice program has announced a bounty of up to $20 million and permanent resettlement for actionable intelligence on Iran’s nuclear program, targeting facilities, hardware, and scientific personnel. The State Department emphasized that Iran remains the only non-nuclear state enriching uranium to 60 percent purity, which could yield material for several nuclear weapons if further enriched, while

Ukrainian Forces Hit 4 Russian Drone Posts in 24 Hours — The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine has announced that Ukrainian forces struck four Russian drone command and control posts within a single 24-hour window across occupied Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Donetsk, and Russia’s Bryansk region. High-value targets included an elite “Rubikon” drone unit base in occupied Berdiansk, alongside posts near Oleshky, Bilytske, and Aleksandrovskoye.
